question: A 16-year-old teenager is brought to the emergency department after having slipped on ice while walking to school. She hit her head on the side of the pavement and retained consciousness. She was brought to the closest ER within an hour of the incident. The ER physician sends her immediately to get a CT scan and also orders routine blood work. The physician understands that in cases of stress, such as in this patient, the concentration of certain hormones will be increased, while others will be decreased. Considering allosteric regulation by hormones, which of the following enzymes will most likely be inhibited in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Stress -> increased certain hormones concentration -> allosteric regulation -> inhibition of Pyruvate carboxylase -> 80% CHAIN: Stress -> increased certain hormones concentration -> allosteric regulation -> inhibition of Phosphofructokinase -> 70% CHAIN: Stress -> increased certain hormones concentration -> allosteric regulation -> inhibition of Glucose-6-phosphatase -> 60% CHAIN: Stress -> increased certain hormones concentration -> allosteric regulation -> inhibition of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase -> 90% CHAIN: Stress -> increased certain hormones concentration -> allosteric regulation -> inhibition of Glycogen phosphorylase -> 80%
analysis: In cases of stress, the body typically activates the fight-or-flight response, leading to an increase in certain hormones like epinephrine and cortisol. These hormones can inhibit the enzyme fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase, which is involved in gluconeogenesis. Inhibition of this enzyme helps divert resources towards immediate energy production rather than glucose synthesis.
